answers.answer: Shuffle the four Conflict III cards and place all of them at the bottom, then shuffle the nine Conflict II cards and deal five on top of them, then shuffle the three Conflict I cards and deal one on top. This makes a 10-card deck ordered I (top), five II, four III. Return unused Conflict cards to the box without looking at them.
answers.evidence: Setup, step 2: ‘Result: a 10-card Conflict Deck — 1 Conflict I on top, 5 Conflict II below it, 4 Conflict III on the bottom. Return the unused Conflict cards to the box without looking at them.’

answers.answer: In a four-player game a human starts at 1 VP; in a three-player game (as in other non-four-player games) at 0 VP. The human starts with two Agents on their Leader and the third Agent, the Swordmaster, beside the board. They have 12 troops total: three in their garrison and nine in supply, in either player count. They start with 1 water in either player count.
answers.evidence: Setup, step 6: ‘Place one of your two discs on the Score track — on the 1 space in a 4-player game, otherwise on the 0 space’; ‘Place two Agents on your Leader and your third Agent (your Swordmaster) next to the game board’; ‘Place three [troops] in one ... garrison ... remaining nine troops in your supply’; ‘Take 1 water.’

answers.answer: Yes. You may take a Reveal turn while you still have Agents, but after revealing you are skipped for the rest of the phase and cannot later take an Agent turn that round. Reveal effects come only from cards revealed from the remaining hand, not cards played on Agent turns. During Clean Up, all cards in front of you from both Agent and Reveal turns go to your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: ‘you may take a Reveal turn while you still have Agents’; ‘Once you've taken a Reveal turn, your turns are skipped for the rest of the phase’; Reveal Turn: effects of ‘just-revealed cards only’; Clean Up moves ‘all cards in front of you (from your Agent and Reveal turns) to your discard pile.’

answers.answer: No. You must pay the destination cost immediately before resolving any effects of the space or the card played; if you cannot pay then, you cannot send the Agent there. One card can send only one Agent, using only one of its Agent icons. A card with no Agent icons cannot be played on an Agent turn; it can only be revealed on a Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn: pay costs ‘immediately (before resolving any effects of the space or the card you played)’; ‘You choose only one Agent icon; one card can't send multiple Agents’; ‘A card with no Agent icons can't be played on an Agent turn.’

answers.answer: At a Combat space, deploy the three troops recruited this turn plus up to two of the four already in your garrison, for a maximum of five. At a non-Combat space, recruited troops stay in the garrison and cannot deploy. Recruited troops come from your supply and are placed in your garrison; at a Combat space, eligible newly recruited troops may then be deployed.
answers.evidence: Recruiting & Deploying Units: the cube icon takes a troop ‘from your supply and place[s] it in your garrison’; at a Combat space deploy ‘any or all units recruited during your current turn ... plus up to two more units from your garrison.’

answers.answer: A Spy Agent icon lets you send an Agent to any space connected to an observation post where you have a Spy; that access does not recall the Spy. Infiltrate recalls your Spy from a connected post to enter a space occupied by another player's Agent. Gather Intelligence recalls a connected Spy to draw a card; choose to do this immediately after placing your Agent and before receiving any space or card effects. The same Spy cannot be used for both effects, though two different Spies can be used for Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence on the same placement.
answers.evidence: Spies & observation posts: Spy Agent icon permits a space connected to a post with your Spy and ‘you do not recall the Spy’; Infiltrate ignores another player's Agent; Gather Intelligence is decided ‘immediately after placing your Agent (before receiving any effects)’; ‘You cannot recall the same Spy to both.’

answers.answer: Strength is 11: two troops contribute 4, one sandworm contributes 3, and four revealed swords contribute 4. If your final unit is removed, your strength becomes 0. With no unit in the Conflict, you cannot join the Combat Intrigue window, which is limited to players with at least one unit in the Conflict.
answers.evidence: Strength: each troop = 2, sandworm = 3, revealed sword = 1; ‘if your last unit is ever removed, your strength becomes 0.’ Combat: only a player with ‘at least one unit in the Conflict’ may play Combat Intrigue cards.

answers.answer: Yes. Passing does not prevent you from acting again; the window closes only after all players involved in Combat pass consecutively. After rewards, troops in the Conflict return to their supply (not their garrison), and all sandworms return to the bank.
answers.evidence: Combat Intrigue: ‘You are not required to pass just because you passed earlier in the phase’; resolve after all involved players ‘pass consecutively.’ Combat cleanup returns troops to ‘supply (not their garrison)’ and sandworms to the bank.

answers.answer: A tie for first means each tied player gets the second reward, but no one wins the Conflict or takes its card. In a four-player game, if exactly two players tie for first, the remaining players compete for the third reward; in a three-player game, no other rewards are given. A player with 0 strength receives no reward.
answers.evidence: Combat ties: tied-for-first players each gain the second reward and ‘no one wins the Conflict or takes the Conflict card’; with three or fewer players no other rewards, while in a four-player game exactly two tied leave the others competing for third. Resolve Combat: ‘A player with 0 strength receives no reward.’

answers.answer: Having one or more sandworms doubles your reward once; two sandworms do not quadruple it. Taking control of a location and battle icons on Conflict cards cannot be doubled. For a reward that lets you pay 3 spice for 1 VP, you may pay the cost a second time to get it again: pay 3 spice for another 1 VP, or 6 spice total for 2 VP under the doubled reward.
answers.evidence: Sandworm Reward Doubling: with ‘one or more sandworms’ double rewards; control and battle icons cannot be doubled. The example says a doubled reward offering 1 VP for 3 spice allows paying ‘3 spice to gain 1 VP, or 6 spice to gain 2.’

answers.answer: Normally, check for a match after winning a Conflict and taking its card into your supply. A face-up Conflict or Objective card in your supply with the same battle icon qualifies; the matching pair must be flipped face down and earns 1 VP. The match is mandatory, not optional. During the Endgame, the wild battle icon can match any one of the three battle icons in your supply; flip that pair face down for 1 VP.
answers.evidence: Battle Icons: when you win and take the card, check for another ‘face-up Conflict or Objective card’; ‘you must flip the matching pair face down and gain 1 VP.’ During Endgame the wild icon matches any one of the three icons.

answers.answer: At 2 Influence, gain 1 VP; lose that VP if Influence falls below 2 and regain it upon reaching 2 again. At 4 Influence, gain the printed track bonus, which is retained if you fall below 4 and earned again upon returning to 4. The first player to 4 also gains the Alliance token and 1 VP; that VP follows possession of the token. Tying the Alliance holder at 4 does not steal it: an opponent must rise higher. If the holder loses Influence after being tied, the formerly tied player takes the Alliance; falling to 3 or lower also loses it, and if no one at 4+ can take it, it returns to the board.
answers.evidence: Victory Points, Faction Influence; FAQ & Rulings, Alliance loss: ‘Tying the current holder does not steal the Alliance’; the formerly tied player takes it if the holder loses Influence after being tied, and falling to 3 or lower loses it.

answers.answer: Persuasion can be spent before, between, or after Reveal effects during your Reveal turn. You may pool Persuasion from multiple sources to buy one card and split Persuasion from one source across different cards. After buying a Row card, its replacement is added immediately, so you may buy that replacement if you can afford it. The acquired card goes face up into your discard pile and is not used right away.
answers.evidence: Reveal Turn: use Persuasion ‘before, between, or after’ Reveal effects. Acquiring Cards: may pool or split Persuasion; the Imperium Row is replenished, so ‘after acquiring a card you may acquire its replacement’; acquired card goes face up into your discard pile.

answers.answer: At each Maker space without an Agent, add 1 spice to its bonus-spice spot; it accumulates with any already there. When you send an Agent to a Maker space, you gain all bonus spice there. The Shield Wall prevents summoning a sandworm to a Conflict at Arrakeen, Spice Refinery, or Imperial Basin while it remains on the board; after it is removed, any Conflict can receive a sandworm. Maker Hooks are normally required when the summoning effect specifies them, but are not universally required if an effect omits them; Hooks are retained rather than spent. A sandworm is placed immediately in your quadrant of the Conflict and can never be put in a garrison.
answers.evidence: Makers phase adds 1 spice at each Agent-free Maker space; sending an Agent gains ‘all the bonus spice there.’ Shield Wall blocks the three named locations. Sandworms: ‘a sandworm can never be placed in a garrison’; Hook requirement is usually specified but ‘not a universal prerequisite.’

answers.answer: At Recall, at the end of the round, 10 or more VP for any player or an empty Conflict Deck triggers the Endgame. Players first play and resolve any Endgame Intrigue cards, then compare Victory Points. The resource tiebreakers in order are spice, Solari, water, then garrisoned troops.
answers.evidence: Phase 5: Recall triggers Endgame if anyone is at 10+ VP or the Conflict Deck is empty. Scoring: first resolve Endgame Intrigue, then most VP wins; tiebreakers are ‘amount of spice, then Solari, then water, then garrisoned troops.’

answers.answer: Standard CHOAM setup uses 20 contracts: two are face up on the board and the remaining 18 are face down in the bank. Add four additional Intrigue cards to the Intrigue Deck and four additional Imperium cards to the Imperium Deck. Shaddam Corrino IV is an optional Leader, not compulsory. The 10 contrasting-back contracts are for Rise of Ix compatibility and stay in the box; they are not part of standard CHOAM setup.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Setup changes: shuffle ‘20 contracts,’ flip two face up, place ‘remaining 18 face down’; shuffle 4 additional Intrigue and 4 Imperium cards into their decks; Shaddam is optional. Contrasting-back section: leave the 10 Rise of Ix contracts in the box for standard CHOAM.

answers.answer: With CHOAM, a contract icon lets you take one of the two face-up contracts into your supply and replace it with a contract from the bank turned face up. If all contracts have been taken, the icon instead gives 2 Solari. A Harvest contract is completed by sending an Agent to a Maker space and gaining the specified amount of spice that turn in total, including spice from other sources. An Immediate contract completes as soon as taken. An Acquire The Spice Must Flow contract completes when you next acquire that card.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Taking contracts and Completing contracts sections: contract icon takes a face-up contract and replaces it; if all have been taken it gives 2 Solari; Harvest, Immediate, and Acquire The Spice Must Flow completion conditions are specified.

answers.answer: No. If you take a contract for a space where you already sent your Agent this turn, you must wait until a future turn; you must have held the contract when you sent the Agent. On completion, announce the contract, gain its shown rewards, flip it face down, and leave it in your supply.
answers.evidence: Completing contracts: for a space where you ‘already sent your Agent this turn,’ wait until a future turn and ‘you must have had the contract at the time you sent your Agent.’ Completion: announce it, gain rewards, flip face down and leave in supply.

answers.answer: Use one shared scoring Rival as the third competitor. The Rival gets the Ornithopter Objective; the two eligible Objectives dealt to the humans determine which human gets the First Player marker. The Rival is considered immediately clockwise from the First Player, making turn order First Player → Rival → other human. First Player alternates only between the humans. The Rival takes Agent turns and never takes a Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: ‘one shared scoring Rival’; give it the Ornithopter Objective and deal the other two eligible Objectives to humans, with First Player based on the card; turn order is First Player → Rival → other human; Rival ‘never takes a Reveal turn.’

answers.answer: If the indicated destination is occupied, the Rival ignores it and reveals another House Hagal card. A Place Spy card uses an empty post of its specified type or ignores placement if none exists; in either case it reveals another Hagal card because it has not sent an Agent. The Rival ignores ordinary board-space costs and effects and applies only the revealed Hagal effects. If House Hagal empties or Reshuffle appears, immediately reshuffle and continue.
answers.evidence: Agent turns: ‘Ignore an occupied destination and reveal again’; empty House Hagal or Reshuffle means immediately reshuffle and continue. Spies and Schemes: Place Spy uses an empty specified post or ignores it, ‘either way reveal another Hagal card because it has not sent an Agent.’ Rival ignores normal space costs/effects and applies only Hagal effects.
